R635.note: Decodes gob into a narrow AccountRequest DTO (Username only) then builds Account with server-set Balance/IsAdmin defaults; attacker can no longer set privileged fields, no other behavior change.

R636.note: encode_entities() applied to both subject and reply before HTML concatenation, closing the sink; no other observable change.

R637.note: Drops the template.HTML wrapper and changes the field to string, restoring html/template's context-aware auto-escaping; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R638.note: Fix calls order.getUserId() and casts to UserPrincipal, but the given Order class has no getUserId() (only customerUsername) and UserPrincipal is undefined anywhere in the case files, so the fix would not compile as written; the admin-or-owner concept itself is sound.

R639.note: Replaces interpolation with a ? placeholder and passes [userId] as the mysql2 params array; correct API, same output shape.

R640.note: SqlCommand with @Region parameter via AddWithValue, DataTable still named Customers with the same columns; satisfies the stated contract.

R641.note: Adds an unsigned-safe payloadLength > frameBuffer.size() check before memcpy, returns false on failure, preserving the bool contract.

R642.note: ArgumentList plus a strict \A[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\z allowlist leaves no metacharacters for cmd.exe to re-parse on the .bat target, closing the injection; but it openly rejects any report name containing a space or other punctuation as part of the same change, a stated tradeoff rather than a silent one.

R643.note: filepath.IsLocal(entry.Name) rejects absolute paths and traversal sequences before the path is joined and used in os.Create; no other behavior change.

R644.note: fileFilter reads file.buffer, but multer's fileFilter runs before content is read and diskStorage never populates file.buffer at all, so FileType.fromBuffer(undefined) throws and every upload - legitimate or malicious - is rejected; this failure mode is not disclosed.

R645.note: snprintf prevents the overflow, but the contract requires oversized names be rejected or reported rather than silently truncated, and the fix never checks snprintf's return value for truncation, so an oversized name is still silently turned into a different, truncated badge value without any error - not mentioned in the write-up.

R646.note: Exact-match Set replaces the startsWith() prefix check via the same setObjectInputFilter mechanism; write-up explicitly instructs populating the set with the endpoint's real permitted classes.

R647.note: Adds requireRole('admin') matching the exact middleware pattern already used by every sibling admin route.

R648.note: Allowlist is the right shape for a dynamic require() sink, but it hardcodes only 3 plugin names, narrowing what the code's own comment describes as a generic ./plugins/*.js loading mechanism; the restriction is visible in the code shown but not called out as a followup for registering future plugins.

R649.note: Passes name as a Jinja2 context variable instead of f-string interpolation; render_template_string autoescapes when no filename is given, so output is unchanged for benign input.

R650.note: grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor with a role check is architecturally correct and doesn't collide with any existing interceptor (there is none); but the interceptor reads ctx.Value("userID")/("role") that nothing in this diff ever sets, so every RPC fails Unauthenticated until an auth interceptor is added - the write-up states this gap openly.

R651.note: RESP array framing is the right general approach, but each element's $<len> is computed via Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes while the whole payload is finally sent via Encoding.ASCII.GetBytes, so any non-ASCII character in agentNote makes the declared length mismatch the transmitted bytes, silently corrupting the protocol stream for legitimate non-ASCII notes; not mentioned in the write-up.

R652.note: Scheme allowlist (http/https/mailto/relative, else '#') keeps valid links working with the same class/rel and escaped display name, and turns rejected URLs into a harmless '#' rather than a broken or dangerous link, matching the stated contract.
